description: Default architecture, no weight assignment (random init, expected ~0% accuracy).

No LayerNorm, float64. Block1: attention reads A, 4-neuron gated MLP makes A*b_j at each multiplier digit. Block2: attention sums partial products minus emitted digits, scaled to [0,10); tropical linear head gives floor(x).

No MLP/ReLU/LayerNorm, float64. Block1: digit-dependent attention log-weights give b*A exactly (softmax as multiplier, with sink). Block2: sum partial products minus emitted digits. Tropical head: floor(remainder/place).
PureAttention_v2 with rectangular attention: 13 registers, per-block heads/key sizes (1 head 3-dim keys, then 2 heads 2-dim keys), scalar values, no sqrt(d) factor.
Sink keeps constant log-weight 0 and queries carry the log-odds log(b/(SA-11111b)), so key rank drops 3->2 and registers 13->11. Block 1 and block 2's prefix head share one digit-address channel.
Partial products and the remainder share one register X (10 registers), since output positions are silenced in block 1. Head is a single tropical formula over all 12 tokens, with no constants.
MergeXPP_v5 with typed registers: token embedding is 2-dim (digit value, log-odds query) and the head reads only (X, PLACE), so a 2-parameter-per-token decoder: k and -k(k+1)/2.
TypedEmbed_v6 with the constant-1 register replaced by a bias on W_q, leaving 9 registers. Queries are now: address constant (bias), digit log-odds QL, step log-scale NL.
QueryBias_v7 with the digit-address channel replaced by a single -1 at the sink position: queries now move weight into or out of the sink instead of touching each digit.
Ablation of SinkAddress_v8: TIE=0. Exact multiples of PLACE tie between adjacent digits in the head.
Ablation of SinkAddress_v8: float32 instead of float64. A 10-digit integer does not fit in 24 mantissa bits.
SinkAddress_v8 with relative Gaussian weight noise of 1e-12, measuring the circuit's numerical margin.
SinkAddress_v8 with relative Gaussian weight noise of 1e-10, measuring the circuit's numerical margin.
SinkAddress_v8 with relative Gaussian weight noise of 1e-11, measuring the circuit's numerical margin.
SinkAddress_v8 with every weight rounded to 12 significant figures: how many decimals does the circuit need?
SinkAddress_v8 with every weight rounded to 10 significant figures: how many decimals does the circuit need?
SinkAddress_v8 with the 'never attend' log-weight OFF=-60 instead of -1000, measuring tolerance to attention leakage.
SinkAddress_v8 with the 'never attend' log-weight OFF=-40 instead of -1000, measuring tolerance to attention leakage.
SinkAddress_v8 with the 'never attend' log-weight OFF=-25 instead of -1000, measuring tolerance to attention leakage.
Ablation of SinkAddress_v8 (OFF=-60): pre-attention LayerNorm restored in both blocks. Mean/std depend on the input, so addresses and values are rescaled per token.
SinkAddress_v8 (OFF=-60) with a standard final LayerNorm kept. Zero-sum head rows cancel its mean and argmax ignores its std, so it is an exact no-op on the decoded digit.
SinkAddress_v8 (OFF=-60) with tie-break 0.05 instead of 0.5: any value in (0,1) should work, up to rounding error.
SinkAddress_v8 (OFF=-60) with a much larger prefix scale SV=1e15: does a mostly-sink attention lose precision?

Huge sinks (SA=1e17, SV=1e22) make softmax act as plain exp, so queries are simply log(b/SA) and the per-step normaliser register disappears: 8 registers and 1-dim keys in block 2. Approximate by design, well inside the 0.5 margin.

LinearSink_v10 with one shared ramp K over multiplicand, sink and output digits (7 registers). The multiplicand is shifted down by e^-100, undone by the digit query in block 1 and invisible to block 2.
Ablation of RampKey_v11: SA=1e12 instead of 1e17. The softmax denominator is no longer constant, so the plain-exp approximation should break.
Ablation of RampKey_v11: SV=1e18 instead of 1e22. The prefix read drifts by about V*sum(places)/SV, roughly 5 at the last digits, breaking them.
RampKey_v11 with SV=1e20. The drift formula V*sum(places)/SV predicts about 0.05, below the 0.5 margin, so this should still pass.
RampKey_v11 with relative weight noise 1e-12, to compare its margin with SinkAddress_v8, which passes at this level.
LinearSink_v10 with relative weight noise 1e-12, to compare its margin with SinkAddress_v8 (passes) and RampKey_v11 (71%).

Final circuit, LinearSink_v10 with knobs removed. Two attention-only blocks: digit queries compute b*A, then partial products minus emitted digits give the long-division remainder; a tropical linear head floors it. No MLP/ReLU/LayerNorm; needs float64.
